subject: Post-demo: Hyperscaler comparison runbook and next tests
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Tayla Reed <tayla@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed comparison runbook

Hi Tayla — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you complete internal buy-in.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary goal: ensure a predictable 99ms p95 for short prompt flows (<=512 tokens) for the recommendation API and compare unit economics.
- Secondary: validate long-context behavior (8k) and cold-start behavior for episodic agents.
- Compliance questions: SOC2 evidence + private VPC options for production.

Proposed lightweight comparison runbook (week-by-week timeline):
1) Baseline (this week, 3 business days): run 1k concurrent requests at batch sizes [1,8,32], measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
2) Resilience (week 2): multi-region failover test (simulate region loss), model-fallback correctness checks, and automated retry behavior.
3) Long-context (week 3): 8k-context generation throughput and KV-cache warm vs cold.
4) Production load (week 4): representative traffic replay (prefix caching enabled) and SLO verification.

Success criteria (suggested):
- p95 latency <= 120ms for single-turn short prompts at batch size 1 (target 99ms).
- Tail stability: p99 spike < 2x baseline p95.
- Cost target: <= 40% of hyperscaler baseline for equivalent throughput (to be measured).
- No data leakage in private deployment test and passing SOC2 evidence checklist.

Owners we suggest at Redwood:
- Karthik Iyer: infra & test harness (throughput, failover, KV-cache scenarios).
- Laura Bennett: SLA & reporting (dashboards, SLO pass/fail).
- Vivek Kulkarni: deal coordination, runbook alignment with Acme priorities.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-checklist.pdf (checklist), comparison-matrix-v1.xlsx (metrics template).

Next steps for Acme: please confirm the primary success metric you want prioritized and any gating procurement dates. If acceptable, Karthik will schedule the first baseline run for Wednesday.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-checklist.pdf pdf)

From: Tayla Reed <tayla@acme.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed comparison runbook

Vivek — this looks great and aligns with what our infra team wanted. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For cost comparisons, we need an apples-to-apples run against their public managed endpoints (GCP Vertex / AWS Bedrock / Azure OpenAI). Can you include the exact model variants you plan to use and the tokenization model so receipts match?
2) SOC2: we need the list of evidence artifacts early (logs, audit trails, KMS key rotation docs).
3) Timeline: procurement has a vendor review on Oct 20. If we can get baseline numbers and a short writeup by Oct 16 it helps.

If Karthik can run baseline Wednesday that works for our team — they will provide a 1-hour window for instance access and a sample traffic trace.

— Tayla
Tayla Reed
VP Product, Acme.ai
(attachment: acme-trace-sample.json json)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tayla Reed <tayla@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed comparison runbook

Thanks — quick technical clarifications and the exact test plan I will execute: 

Test harness details (what Redwood will run against each target):
- Model variants: open_flan_2_7b (quantized int8 where supported) for Redwood-hosted; for hyperscalers we'll run the closest public variant used in the demo (to be enumerated: Vertex-sim-7b, Bedrock-7b-sim).
- Tokenization: use GPT2 tokenizer canonicalization script (attached link in Drive).
- Workloads: 3 workloads — small prompts (<=512), long context (8k), streaming token output (chat completions).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, max sustainable RPS, error rates, cost per 1M tokens (raw compute + platform fees where available).
- Cold vs warm: run 3 cold restarts, then warm with 10k prefix cache replay.

Schedule & owners:
- Baseline run: Wednesday 2026-10-06 10:00-11:30 PT (I'll coordinate infra). Vivek — can you confirm Redwood test credentials and the test script repo access?
- Ingestion of Acme trace: Tayla to drop the sample trace in the Drive folder by EOD Monday.
- SOC2 artifacts: Laura will attach initial evidence list (logs retention window, KMS integration notes) by Monday COB.

Quick note on hyperscaler comparators: we will avoid deep production networking parity tests (e.g., private peering) in the baseline. Those are covered in a later stage private deployment run. Baseline keeps networking to public endpoints so we measure managed endpoint economics.

I'll share the raw CSV metrics and a short one-page executive summary after the baseline run.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference Reliability
Redwood Inference
(attachment: comparison-matrix-v1.xlsx xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tayla Reed <tayla@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed comparison runbook

All set from my side. I've uploaded the SOC2 evidence checklist and a Dashboard template to the Drive folder. Quick operational points: 

- SLA gating: if baseline shows p95 <= 120ms and error rate <0.1% under representative load, we mark "SLA candidate" and start drafting contract terms.
- Reporting: I'll publish a per-test dashboard with pass/fail flags and a short narrative.
- Escalation: if any repro shows data isolation or encryption gaps, we will pause public results and run private VPC verification.

Vivek — please confirm you have the Redwood service tokens ready for Wednesday and I will loop in support for any on-call needs.

Thanks everyone,
Laura
Senior Product Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
